content:
maria: Heads-up — customer (gov-health org) escalated: they want per-request audit bundles delivered over SFTP, each bundle signed, and the request payloads encrypted with a customer-managed KEK (KMS-wrapped). They also asked for explicit event-level RBAC identity (actor_role) for every admin action. Renewal meeting Friday, need clear ask/impact + SLA language.

dan: Ok. Main concerns: 1) Delivery SLA & manifest signing, 2) exposing per-event actor_role means adding fields to schema + backfill for historical events, 3) KMS-wrapped keys for request payloads — we can do envelope encryption but we cannot hand over CMKs.

sara: +1 to Dan. For schema, propose adding these fields: actor_role, actor_id_hash, event_signature, kms_encrypted_dek. We should include event_hash so customers can validate integrity without us handing over raw keys.

owen: For KMS: we can support customer KEK wrapping via envelope encryption: generate DEK per-bundle, wrap with customer-provided public key (or use customer KMS to wrap). Implementation options: 1) customer provides a wrapKey endpoint (risky), 2) we call customer KMS (requires cross-account permissions), 3) we accept a customer-wrapped DEK blob they upload to the bundle request. Option 3 is simplest from our side.

owen: Example audit event snippet we'd add to schema (minimal):
```json
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-15T14:21:00Z",
  "actor": "alice@example.com",
  "actor_role": "org:admin",
  "action": "grant_role",
  "resource": "project:payroll-db",
  "request_id": "req-12345",
  "event_hash": "sha256:...",
  "event_signature": "sig:...",
  "kms_encrypted_dek": "base64(...)"
}
```

sara: Runtime impact: adding signing per-event will increase CPU and storage (signed payloads + index). We'll need a job to sign/attach signatures to historical events if customer requests backfill — cost estimate: ~4-6 hours infra work + >24h of batch for 30M events.

tim-legal: On SLA/contract: what timeline are we comfortable promising for evidence delivery? Customer asked for 48h delivery for on-demand bundles and 7-day retention for staging bundles. Also need to confirm liability and data residency clauses. We should avoid promising KMS key custody; prefer language: "support customer-provided wrapped keys" and "deliver signed bundles within 72 hours" unless Eng confirms faster.

maria: Noted. For FedRAMP/HIPAA overlap: we need to make sure PII in events is redacted by default unless customer explicitly opts in and provides justification + BAAs. Also, how does this change incident response? If audit shows suspected exfil, do we have an on-call playbook that includes preserving the KEKs and not rotating keys until investigation?

owen: Incident triage note — if bundle contains potential exfil indicators: 1) snapshot current infra (VMs, GPUs), 2) freeze further bundle generation for that tenant, 3) escalate to IR + legal, 4) preserve chain-of-custody: store signed manifest + event hashes in an immutable bucket (WORM). We should not require customer KEK for preservation; we'll store wrapped DEKs as-is.

security-bot: Reminder: current retention policy (eng-security policy v2) keeps audit logs 1 year by default; special retention requests must be in contract. See: https://redwood.internal/policies/audit-retention

dan: I'll spin up a proof-of-concept branch with schema + bundle manifest format. Link will follow: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/xxxx (WIP). Will add an integration test that verifies event_signature verification with a sample public key.

sara: We'll need an ops runbook entry documenting performance impact and a migration plan for historical events (opt-in backfill only). Suggest a cross-team sync Wed 10am to align infra/eng-ml/legal.

maria: Thanks all — I'll draft the customer response with conservative SLA language (72h for ad-hoc bundles, 30d for on-demand huge backfills, opt-in backfill only) and attach the sample schema + options. @tim-legal can you review contract wording after we have the draft? :pray:

tim-legal: Will review. Please include indemnity and data-residency constraints in the draft.

maria: Great. Meeting invite sent. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
